content: The international aspects of the topic will be documented in the guideline. Dr. André Briend, a highly experienced researcher, program manager, and pediatrician, was a member of the technical staff in the Department of Child and Adolescent Health and Development at the World Health Organization (WHO) until 2010. He currently works as an independent consultant. Dr. Briend contributed to the development of the patent for the ready-to-use therapeutic food (RUTF) known as Plumpy’Nut. However, he does not own the rights to this product and does not receive royalties. The patent is owned by Nutriset and the Institut de Recherche pour le Développement. It was agreed that this information would be included in the guideline. Dr. Mark Manary is a Professor of Pediatrics at Washington University School of Medicine in St. Louis, USA, and serves as the director of the Global Harvest Alliance, a collaboration between St. Louis Children’s Hospital and the Donald Danforth Plant Science Center. His research focuses on various aspects of nutrition in populations from developing countries, particularly in Malawi, Africa. Over the past three years, Dr. Manary has been active in academia and is the founder of the non-governmental organization Project Peanut Butter. This organization produces RUTF for use in programs in Malawi and Sierra Leone. Project Peanut Butter operates as a charitable initiative, selling RUTF on a cost-recovery basis to governments and agencies, which then distribute it free of charge to malnourished children. It was determined that Dr. Manary’s humanitarian work with Project Peanut Butter would also be reported in the guideline. The guideline development process includes plans for updating the recommendations. A review of the global guideline is scheduled for 2020. If new information becomes available at that time, a guideline review group will be convened to assess the evidence and revise the recommendations accordingly. The Department of Nutrition for Health and Development at WHO headquarters in Geneva, in collaboration with internal partners, will oversee the coordination of the guideline update following the formal procedures outlined in the WHO Handbook for Guideline Development. WHO also welcomes suggestions for additional questions to be evaluated during the guideline review process.
